title: Severe tinnitus distress with insomnia and anxiety

stages.title: 1. Extract the clinical story
stages.prompt: Which additional impact information is most important?

options.text: Severity of distress, sleep disruption, anxiety, daily functioning and current supports

stages.feedback: The specified case emphasizes severe distress, insomnia and anxiety, so functional and psychosocial impact is central.

stages.title: 2. Interpret the findings
stages.prompt: The case includes moderate flat SNHL and a high tinnitus-impact score. What should the student recognize?

options.text: Tinnitus distress is clinically significant and requires an individualized audiological and psychosocial management plan
The hearing loss alone explains every aspect of distress
A high score means the tinnitus must be objectively measurable

stages.feedback: The case is designed to separate tinnitus impact from audiometric severity and to encourage holistic management.

stages.title: 3. Check for red flags and safety
stages.prompt: How should severe distress be handled?

options.text: Assess safety and psychosocial needs, and escalate appropriately if an immediate mental-health concern is identified
Assume anxiety is irrelevant to tinnitus care
Treat the audiogram and skip psychosocial screening

stages.feedback: Severe distress requires attention to safety and appropriate co-management; the case should not assume an emergency without evidence.

stages.title: 4. Select management
stages.prompt: Which plan best matches the specified case?

options.text: Tinnitus counselling/education and sound-based support with consideration of CBT-informed psychological co-management and hearing needs

stages.feedback: The protocol specifically calls for counselling/sound therapy with psychological co-management considerations.

stages.title: 5. Justify the decision
stages.prompt: Which justification best links the findings to management?

options.text: High tinnitus distress with sleep and anxiety impact warrants a person-centred plan addressing tinnitus, hearing and psychosocial needs together
Psychological factors should never be discussed in tinnitus care
The same intervention is suitable regardless of distress level

stages.feedback: The learning objective is integrated management rather than treating the tinnitus signal in isolation.

stages.title: 6. Plan follow-up

options.text: Tinnitus impact, sleep, distress/anxiety, hearing-related difficulties, adherence and patient-reported benefit

stages.feedback: Follow-up should use meaningful patient-centred outcomes, including distress and sleep impact.
